# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, Unconfirmed... At risk Correction on the band: confidence is High (checked 21 of 23 points), so the band comes from the low number. **46–54/100, At risk.** Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. Most checks could be read from code. Three things are costing points: the app renders only in the browser, `/guides` is marked noindex, and `/guides` is reachable only through a button. The one unknown is the canonical link (GEO-015), because the site's domain isn't declared. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Turn on server rendering (GEO-003, 3 points lost) - **Why it matters:** with `ssr: false`, the server sends an empty shell and the text appears only after JavaScript runs. Many crawlers don't run JavaScript, so they may see no content. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small (set it to `true`, or prerender the pages) - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Stop marking `/guides` as noindex (GEO-014, 1.5 points lost) - **Why it matters:** `/guides` is in your sitemap and is your main content page, but the server tells search engines to ignore it. That is a mixed signal. - **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` - **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` - **Size:** Small (remove the middleware, or limit it to `/admin`) - **Score after this:** 52–61 ### 3. Link to `/guides` with a real link (GEO-016, 2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** crawlers follow `` links. They don't click buttons, so `/guides` may never be discovered through navigation. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small (use ``) - **Score after this:** 54–63 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sane size | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and its lines are valid | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks only `/admin`. No config, so I assumed you want to be found | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | 1 of 2 routes clear. `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` noindexes `/guides`. `/admin` is deliberately noindex and isn't in the sitemap, so I left it out | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your domain | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical anywhere, and no site origin is declared in `nuxt.config.ts` | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2` `ssr: false`, which affects every route | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4` `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` is relative, and it must be absolute | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | Not run | `lang` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5`, but the title (`app.vue:2`) and description (`nuxt.config.ts:6`) are the same on both routes | | GEO-016 | Pages reachable by real links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8` is the only path to `/guides`, and it is a button | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` in the files I read | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read `app.vue` and all three pages. There are no images, and the button has text | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. Not scored | ## Other problems found - **Sitemap lists a noindexed page:** `public/sitemap.xml:4` `https://trailhead.example/guides`. The middleware at `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` noindexes it. Fixing item 2 resolves this. - **Sitemap host looks like a placeholder:** `public/sitemap.xml:3` `https://trailhead.example/`. Use the real production domain, and use the same one in `robots.txt` and canonicals. ## Worth considering - **`/guides` promises more than it delivers:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. The page lists no routes and no grades. Adding the actual routes as text, each with its own page, might give readers and machines something to quote. - **The home page says little:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. Beyond the heading and one button, no walk or area is described in text. - **Give each page its own title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' })`. Use `useHead` or `useSeoMeta` in each page, for example "Trail guides | Trailhead". ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 canonical:** no site origin is declared. Tell me your production domain (the sitemap suggests `trailhead.example`) and I can treat this as a clear Problem or Clear. - **Sitemap URLs:** whether the listed URLs answer 200 is live-only. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. - `/admin` is meant to stay private, so its noindex and the `Disallow: /admin` line are deliberate. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
